description: United States: can I retire at 62 with $800k (or any age and balance)? Year by year to 95 for one person or a married couple: 401(k)/traditional IRA contributions off income tax (2027 limit $25,500, catch-up $8,500 at 50+, $11,750 at 60-63) and FICA on pay, withdrawals from 60 (59 1/2), required minimum distributions from 75 on the Uniform Lifetime Table, Social Security from the claiming age (62 = 70%, 67 = 100%, 70 = 124% for people born 1960+), federal tax with the 2027 brackets, the extra standard deduction at 65+, the senior deduction ($6,000, 2025-2028) and the tax on Social Security (Pub 915), an optional flat state rate and a UK State Pension. Returns the age the money lasts to, wealth at retirement, the spending that lasts to 95, a retire-at-60/62/65 comparison and key years in today’s money.
